title: Coaching Has Outgrown Ad Hoc. Here's What Comes Next.
summary: New survey data shows a widening gap between organizations that coach consistently and those that don't. Here's how Ambition is closing it.
body_markdown:
Ask a revenue leader how pipeline is trending, and they'll have an answer instantly. Ask them how many of their managers actually coached this week — and whether that coaching was any good — and the confidence tends to drop off fast.


That gap isn't a leadership failure. It's an infrastructure failure. Most organizations have spent years building systems to make pipeline visible, predictable, and inspectable. Coaching, meanwhile, has often been left to run on instinct, calendar invites, and whatever structure an individual manager happens to bring to the job.


This summer, Ambition surveyed over 300 revenue leaders across industries to see just how wide that gap has become — and it's wider than most would guess.


To dive deeper,[download the complete State of Sales Coaching Report here](https://ambition.com/resources/the-state-of-sales-coaching-in-2026) .


## The Data Behind the Gap


Only 30% of organizations coach on a weekly or bi-weekly cadence. The rest rely on monthly, quarterly, or ad hoc coaching — or don't have a defined cadence at all. Even among organizations with a coaching framework on paper, 35% describe the quality of that coaching as highly variable across managers, and another 12% have no way to measure coaching quality whatsoever.


The organizations on the right side of that gap aren't succeeding by accident. Ambition customers are twice as likely to have consistent coaching quality across their manager team, nearly twice as likely to reach the majority of reps with weekly structured coaching, and 60% more likely to say leadership is confident coaching is happening consistently and well. That consistency shows up downstream in quota attainment, not just manager satisfaction scores.


The pattern is clear: coaching that's structured, cadenced, and visible outperforms coaching that isn't. **Coaching in Ambition works – and ours just got a major upgrade.**


## A Simpler Foundation: Four Core Objects


The biggest change under the hood is how coaching itself is structured, moving to four clearly defined coaching objects: **Sessions** for single touchpoints, **Programs** for recurring 1:1 or group coaching, **Managed Programs** for recurring coaching with org-level oversight built in, and **Cadences** for step-based coaching with a defined start and end.


Nothing about the underlying coaching motion disappeared; it's just organized into a clearer, more consistent set of objects.


## One Form, Multiple Outputs


Creating any of those objects now runs through the same guided flow. You start by choosing a template or starting fresh. From there, you assign the session as either a 1:1 or a group check-in, determine who it's for, then layer in agenda items, co-coaches, and rating criteria. One flow, four possible outputs. This matters more than it sounds, because the fastest way to kill a coaching habit is to make the admin around it heavier than the conversation itself.


## Easier to Find, Easier to Navigate


Navigation got a refresh too: an improved left-hand nav, the ability to move fluidly between Sessions and Programs, and breadcrumbs that track exactly where you are in the flow.


Session cards also got more informative. You can now see scheduling details, session format, and who's involved — both the managing coach and participants — along with status, all directly on the card.


## Removing the Friction Around the Conversation


Structure solves half the problem. The other half is everything that happens around the actual coaching conversation — scheduling it, finding the link, or remembering it's on the calendar at all.


Ambition's new two-way calendar sync addresses that directly. Managers and reps can now sync their Google or Outlook calendars, compare real availability when scheduling a session, and edit an individual's meeting time within a program without disrupting the rest of the group. Zoom integration means a meeting link gets added with a single click — or, for teams on a different platform, a manual link works just as well — and either way, it travels straight to the participant's calendar and into their Ambition agenda, so joining a session is a click, not a search.


It's a small-sounding change with an outsized effect: every point of friction removed from getting into a coaching conversation is one less excuse not to have it.


## Where Coaching Is Headed


The next frontier is making the conversation itself — not just the scheduling around it — part of the system. Ambition's team is exploring how to bring the actual coaching dialogue back into the platform, whether through transcripts, live feeds, or call recordings, so managers spend less time filling out post-session notes and more time acting on what was actually said.


Paired with that is a deeper focus on coaching effectiveness: not just whether coaching happened, but whether it moved the outcomes leaders are actually accountable for. And as Ambition's Agentic experience rolls out more broadly, that data becomes something leaders can query directly — one-click Skills that surface a team's performance themes from the last week, customizable to whatever a leader needs visibility into, whether that's coaching consistency, rep performance, or lagging indicators tied to revenue.


None of this replaces the manager. It's aimed at the opposite problem — giving managers back the time and context that currently gets lost to admin work, so more of their week goes toward the reps who actually need it.


## Closing the Gap


The coaching black box has never been a mystery of intent. Leaders know coaching matters; the data above confirms it. The gap has always been about visibility and structure — whether an organization can actually see coaching happening, inspect its quality, and improve it the same way it inspects a forecast.


That's the bar Ambition is building toward: coaching that's as structured, visible, and improvable as every other lever revenue leaders already manage closely.


This is just the start of what we learned in the State of Sales Coaching survey.[Download the full report here](https://ambition.com/resources/the-state-of-sales-coaching-in-2026) .
